_metadata.description: Pre-computed ground track data for major satellites and access window analysis
_metadata.computation_method: Simplified two-body + J2 secular perturbation model (not full SGP4). Positions are approximate; suitable for educational visualisation.
sources: Access geometry from Wertz & Larson (1999) Space Mission Engineering: The New SMAD
notes: Ground tracks are historical snapshots valid near the reference epoch.
Actual current positions differ — regenerate via scripts/generate_orbital_data.py.
Longitude values in degrees East (positive East, negative West).
Step size: 60 seconds per point for all ground tracks.

ground_stations.name: KSAT Svalbard Ground Station (SvalSat)
ground_stations.notes: Near-polar location (78°N) allows contact with every SSO pass — up to 12–14 passes/day for 700-km SSO

ground_tracks.description: ISS ground track — 3 orbits (~93 min each), showing westward drift of ~22.5° per orbit due to Earth rotation
Hubble ground track — low inclination (28.47°) stays in tropical/subtropical band. ~95 min period.
Sentinel-2A SSO ground track — retrograde inclination (98.57°) gives near-polar coverage. Period ~100.6 min.

windows.notes: Near-overhead pass; high elevation for polar orbit at 78°N station
